statement: NetBench asks five research questions about adaptation mechanism, heterogeneity across models, retrieval versus parametric adaptation, the gap to frontier APIs and its cost, and measurement rigor. It compares up to eight variants per model (instruct, LoRA SFT, full SFT, CPT plus SFT, LoRA CPT plus SFT, and three retrieval variants) and fixes its statistics in advance: paired Wilcoxon tests, Benjamini–Hochberg correction at q = 0.05, and a practical-significance rule requiring a change of at least 0.25 on the 1–5 scale, an effect size d_z of at least 0.2, and significance. The benchmark has splits of 200 test, 30 dev, 8 adversarial, and 4 synthesis items; difficulty of 77 easy, 99 medium, and 66 hard set by a three-model calibration ladder that overrode the generator's label on 144 of 242 items; and 10 categories. All three authors reviewed every question, which removed 9. The models are llama-3.2-1b, gemma-3-1b, qwen3.5-2b, llama-3.1-8b, qwen3.5-9b, gemma-3-12b, gemma-3-27b, and qwen3.5-27b, with gpt-4o, gemini-2.5-pro, and claude-sonnet-4-6 as API baselines.
evidence: https://github.com/NiebHasan077/NetBench BENCHMARK_CARD.md and docs/STUDY_DESIGN.md; owner approved on 2026-10-07
